record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers
record.original_question: Let f be a balanced Boolean function. Is there a general relationship between the annihilator ideal AN(f) of functions g satisfying g(x)f(x)=0 for all x and the annihilator ideal AN(1+f) of functions annihilating the complement of f?

evidence.quote: Definition 1. Let f be a Boolean function of n variables. The annihilator ideal of f, denoted by AN(f), is the set of all Boolean functions g of n variables such that g(x)f(x)=0, ∀x ∈ Fn 2 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Boolean function f : F_2^n → F_2, define its annihilator ideal
   AN(f) = { g : F_2^n → F_2 such that g(x) f(x) = 0 for every x ∈ F_2^n }.
Note that AN(1+f) is then the set of Boolean functions annihilating the complement 1+f of f, i.e. functions vanishing on the support of 1+f.

A Boolean function f is called balanced if |{x ∈ F_2^n : f(x) = 1}| = 2^(n-1).

Problem: For every balanced Boolean function f, determine whether there exists a general structural relationship between the two annihilator ideals AN(f) and AN(1+f) (for example, a bijection, a degree-preserving correspondence, or an algebraic identity relating their members or their minimum-degree elements), and describe such a relationship explicitly if it exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results discuss annihilators of f and 1+f in the context of algebraic immunity and algebraic attacks on stream ciphers, noting that finding low-degree annihilators of both f and 1+f is central but generally hard. No source explicitly establishes a general structural relationship between AN(f) and AN(1+f) for arbitrary balanced f, nor a proof that none exists. The problem appears to remain unresolved in the cited literature.

status_evidence.title: Basic Theory in Construction of Boolean Functions with Maximum Possible Annihilator Immunity
status_evidence.snippet: The main objective is to find out minimum (or low) degree annihilators of f and 1 + f, i.e., to find out minimum (or low) degree n-variable nonzero functions g1, g2 such that f * g1 = 0 and (1+f) * g2 = 0.
status_evidence.claim: AN(f) and AN(1+f) are studied jointly via algebraic immunity but no general structural relation is established.

status_evidence.title: On the Annihilators of Boolean Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the annihilator ideal of Boolean polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on annihilator ideals does not give an explicit general relation between AN(f) and AN(1+f) for balanced f.
